name: Food Delivery (DoorDash / Uber Eats)
description: Design a food delivery platform like DoorDash or Uber Eats. Covers real-time order tracking, driver dispatch optimization, restaurant integration, and ETA estimation.

learnSteps.title: Order Flow Architecture
learnSteps.description: When a customer places an order, the Order Service validates it (menu availability, pricing, address), processes payment, and publishes an OrderCreated event to Kafka. This event-driven design decouples order placement from restaurant notification and driver dispatch.

learnSteps.title: Driver Dispatch Optimization
learnSteps.description: The Dispatch Worker consumes order events and matches them with available drivers. It uses a geospatial index (Redis GEO or H3 hexagonal grid) to find nearby drivers. The matching algorithm optimizes for minimizing total delivery time across all active orders, considering driver location, restaurant prep time, and traffic.

learnSteps.title: Real-Time Order Tracking
learnSteps.description: Drivers publish GPS locations every 4 seconds. These locations update a Redis GEO set for dispatch and are pushed to customers via WebSocket/SSE. The order state machine (placed, accepted, preparing, picked_up, delivering, delivered) transitions are stored in PostgreSQL and broadcast in real-time.

learnSteps.title: Restaurant and Menu Caching
learnSteps.description: Restaurant menus, hours, and availability are cached in Redis with a 30-minute TTL. Restaurants update menus via a dashboard, invalidating the cache. Popular restaurants near a user are pre-fetched. Image assets (food photos) are stored in S3 and served via CDN.

chaosScenarios.name: Dinner-Rush Dispatch Backlog
chaosScenarios.description: Friday 7pm order surge outpaces the dispatch workers; the driver-matching pipeline falls behind the order event stream
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Kafka consumer lag grows steadily; time-to-assign climbs from ~30s to 10+ minutes. Orders sit unassigned while food is ready, restaurants stack completed bags, customers cancel, and cancellations generate refund load on the order service.
mitigationSteps: Scale the dispatch consumer group toward the 64-partition ceiling
Degrade matching from batch optimization to greedy nearest-driver to cut per-order compute
Widen the dispatch radius and surface longer ETAs instead of accepting orders that cannot be served
Throttle order intake per zone (mark saturated restaurants as temporarily unavailable)

chaosScenarios.name: PostgreSQL Primary Failover
chaosScenarios.description: The orders database primary crashes mid-peak, forcing replica promotion while order writes are in flight
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Order placement and state-machine transitions fail for 15-60s during promotion. In-flight payments complete against orders that never persisted unless idempotency keys are honored on retry. Tracking screens freeze on the last stored state.
mitigationSteps: Automatic replica promotion with the app retrying writes using idempotency keys
Replay missed state transitions from the Kafka order event log
Reconcile payment captures against persisted orders after recovery

chaosScenarios.name: Driver Location Pipeline Degradation
chaosScenarios.description: The Redis GEO tier slows under load; 4-second driver location updates back up and the live index goes stale
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Dispatch matches against positions that are 30-120s old: drivers get assigned to pickups they have already driven away from, ETAs drift badly, and customer tracking maps jump or freeze. Menu reads sharing the same cache also slow down.
mitigationSteps: Fall back to last-known position plus heading extrapolation for matching
Reduce location update frequency adaptively for idle drivers to shed write load
Split menu caching and the GEO index onto separate Redis clusters so one cannot starve the other

bottleneckProgression.description: Order writes, state transitions, and tracking reads exhaust the 500-connection pool
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Add PgBouncer transaction pooling and route tracking reads to the 3 replicas

bottleneckProgression.description: Batch matching is compute-heavy; order events outpace worker throughput at meal peaks
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Scale the consumer group and switch to greedy matching when lag exceeds the SLO

bottleneckProgression.description: GPS writes every 4s per driver plus menu reads saturate the shared Redis endpoint
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Enable cluster mode with zone-keyed GEO shards; isolate menus from location data

expectedIssues.title: Meal-Time Thundering Peaks
expectedIssues.description: Traffic runs 5-8x baseline for two predictable windows a day; static capacity is wasteful and reactive autoscaling lags the lunch spike
expectedIssues.mitigation: Scheduled pre-scaling ahead of 11:30 and 18:00 local peaks layered under reactive policies

expectedIssues.title: Order Topic as Critical Dispatch Path
expectedIssues.description: Every order reaches drivers only through the Kafka topic; broker loss or an under-replicated partition silently stalls dispatch for affected zones
expectedIssues.mitigation: Replication factor 3 across AZs, min.insync.replicas=2, and alerting on time-to-assign rather than broker health alone

expectedIssues.title: Hot-Zone Dispatch Saturation
expectedIssues.description: A stadium event or storm concentrates orders in one geographic zone; its partition backlog grows while other zones idle
expectedIssues.mitigation: Zone-keyed partitioning with per-zone lag monitoring, plus demand throttling and driver incentives for the hot zone

expectedIssues.title: Menu Cache Stampede at Peak Open
expectedIssues.description: Popular restaurants opening at 11:00 expire their cached menus simultaneously, sending a read burst to PostgreSQL
expectedIssues.mitigation: Jittered TTLs, request coalescing, and stale-while-revalidate for menu reads

expectedIssues.title: GPS Write Amplification
expectedIssues.description: 100k active drivers at a 4s update interval is ~25k location writes/sec into Redis before a single customer request is served
expectedIssues.mitigation: Adaptive update intervals (slower when idle or stationary) and regional GEO set sharding

Scale the dispatch consumer group toward the partition count
Flip matching to greedy nearest-driver mode to cut per-order compute
Coordinate with live ops: pause promos, enable longer-ETA messaging, throttle saturated zones

decisions.title: Event-Driven Order Lifecycle
decisions.context: Order placement, restaurant notification, and driver dispatch have different latency budgets and independent failure modes
decisions.decision: Publish OrderCreated to Kafka and let dispatch consume asynchronously rather than dispatching inline with checkout
consequences: Order placement stays fast even when matching is backed up
Dispatch delay becomes a queue-lag problem that needs its own SLO and alerting

decisions.title: Redis GEO as the Live Driver Index
decisions.context: Matching needs nearby-driver radius queries against positions refreshed every 4 seconds across the whole fleet
decisions.decision: Keep live driver positions in Redis GEO sets keyed by zone; PostgreSQL stores only durable order and user state
consequences: Sub-millisecond radius queries at dispatch time without touching the transactional database
Driver positions are ephemeral — a cache incident immediately degrades matching quality

decisions.title: Batch-Window Matching
decisions.context: Greedy per-order assignment is locally optimal but produces poor marketplace-wide delivery times when orders and drivers are dense
decisions.decision: Dispatch workers match orders to drivers in short batch windows, optimizing total delivery time across concurrent orders
consequences: Better fleet utilization and ETAs at peak density
Every order pays a small assignment-delay floor of one batch window, even off-peak

tradeoffs.choice: Short batch windows over instant greedy assignment
tradeoffs.benefit: Lower total delivery time and better driver utilization across the marketplace
tradeoffs.cost: A deliberate 5-15s delay before any driver is assigned

tradeoffs.choice: 4-second GPS updates into Redis, never PostgreSQL
tradeoffs.benefit: Tens of thousands of location writes per second stay off the transactional database
tradeoffs.cost: Positions can be seconds stale, and a durable location trail requires separate archiving

alternatives.name: Synchronous Dispatch in the Order Path
alternatives.description: Find and assign a driver inside the order placement request before responding to the customer
alternatives.prosVsCons: Simplest flow with instant assignment feedback, but couples checkout latency and availability to driver search — one slow match stalls order placement
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Meal-time peaks make matching the slowest and most variable step; it cannot sit on the checkout critical path

alternatives.name: Per-City Deployment Silos
alternatives.description: Run an independent stack per metro area for isolation
alternatives.prosVsCons: Blast-radius isolation and data locality, but N× operational overhead and inevitable configuration drift between cities
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Zone-keyed Kafka partitions deliver most of the isolation benefit without separate stacks
